[package]
name = "mbrotli"
version = "0.4.1-baseline"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.89"
license = "MIT"
description = "Fast Brotli (RFC 7932 and RFC 9841) compression and decompression in safe Rust; encoding is byte-identical to Google's reference encoder"
repository = "https://github.com/Mnwa/mbrotli"
homepage = "https://github.com/Mnwa/mbrotli"
documentation = "https://docs.rs/mbrotli"
readme = "README.md"
keywords = ["brotli", "compression", "encoder", "simd"]
categories = ["compression", "algorithms", "no-std"]
exclude = [
    ".github/**",
    "architecture/**",
    "benchmarks/**",
    "brotli-ffi/**",
    "docs/**",
    "fuzz/**",
    "specifications/**",
    "target/**",
]

[dependencies.fearless_simd]
version = "0.7"
optional = true
default-features = false

[dependencies.thiserror]
version = "2"
optional = true
default-features = false

[dependencies.libm]
version = "0.2"
optional = true

# Profiling instrumentation only. Optional so an ordinary dependant never pulls
# the proc-macro crate into its tree; every `#[hotpath::measure]` anchor in
# `src/` is written as `#[cfg_attr(feature = "hotpath", hotpath::measure)]`.
[dependencies.hotpath]
version = "0.25"
optional = true

[dev-dependencies]
rayon = "1.12"
tempfile = "3.27"

# Retain the independent scalar oracle only for development builds.
[dev-dependencies.fearless_simd]
version = "0.7"
default-features = false
features = ["force_support_fallback", "std"]

[dev-dependencies.criterion]
version = "0.8"

[dev-dependencies.google-brotli-ffi]
path = "/home/mnwa/projects/mbrotli/brotli-ffi"

[[bench]]
name = "compress"
harness = false
required-features = ["compression"]

[[bench]]
name = "track_b"
harness = false
required-features = ["compression", "experimental"]

[features]
default = ["std", "compression", "decompression"]
# Independently selectable public codecs and their private implementations.
compression = ["dep:fearless_simd", "dep:thiserror"]
decompression = ["dep:fearless_simd", "dep:thiserror"]
# Dependency runtime detection for ordinary builds.
std = ["fearless_simd?/std", "thiserror?/std"]
# Opt-in alloc-backed support; overrides std-only APIs and instrumentation.
# Disable default features too when targeting a platform without std.
no_std = ["dep:libm", "fearless_simd?/libm"]

# RFC 9841's shared dictionary and framing formats, which are specified but
# have no stable reference encoder: the C library compiles its serialized
# dictionary parser out unless `BROTLI_EXPERIMENTAL` is defined, and it has no
# framing writer at all. Everything gated here is therefore validated against
# the RFC and against this crate's own decoder-independent fixtures rather than
# against byte identity with a pinned C encoder, which is the guarantee the
# default surface rests on. The API behind this gate may change in a patch
# release; the default surface may not.
#
# Enabling it also builds the vendored C library with `BROTLI_EXPERIMENTAL`, so
# the differential tests have an oracle for the serialized dictionary format.
experimental = ["google-brotli-ffi/experimental"]

# Exposes the prepared-dictionary longest-match diagnostic. It answers how well
# a candidate dictionary covers a corpus, which is worth knowing before
# shipping one, but the candidate order it breaks ties by is an implementation
# detail; keeping it behind a feature keeps that out of the default surface.
diagnostics = []

# `hotpath` turns the measurement anchors on; the two mode features add a
# sampling mode on top of it, so each implies `hotpath` rather than standing
# alone with an inert runtime.
hotpath = ["dep:hotpath", "hotpath/hotpath"]
hotpath-cpu = ["hotpath", "hotpath/hotpath-cpu"]
hotpath-alloc = ["hotpath", "hotpath/hotpath-alloc"]

from pathlib import Path
import subprocess, os, json, shutil, time

artifacts = root / 'target/encoder-optimization'

history = []

def run(name, args, *, env=None, output=None):
    print('START', name, flush=True)
    begin = time.time()
    with (output or artifacts / (name + '.log')).open('w') as log:
        subprocess.run(args, cwd=root, stdout=log, stderr=log, check=True, env=env)
    history.append({'name': name, 'args': list(map(str,args)), 'start': begin, 'end': time.time()})
    (artifacts / 'measurement-final-history.json').write_text(json.dumps(history, indent=2) + '\n')
    print('DONE', name, flush=True)

run('criterion-final', ['taskset', '-c', '2', artifacts / 'comparison-final', '--bench',
    '--save-baseline', 'encoder-final-20260914', '--sample-size', '20',

from pathlib import Path
import csv,statistics
from collections import defaultdict
p=Path('docs/benchmarks/encoder-optimization-2026-09-14')
def read(name):return list(csv.DictReader((p/name).open()))
pairs=read('paired-summary.csv')
primary={(r['corpus'],int(r['quality']),r['mode']):r for r in pairs if r['suite']=='primary'}
heldout={(r['corpus'].split('/')[-1],int(r['quality'])):r for r in pairs if r['suite']=='heldout'}
def ratio(r):return f"{float(r['speedup']):.3f}×"
def interval(r):return f"{float(r['speedup_lower']):.3f}–{float(r['speedup_upper']):.3f}"
def table(headers,rows):return '| '+' | '.join(headers)+' |\n| '+' | '.join(['---']*len(headers))+' |\n'+''.join('| '+' | '.join(map(str,row))+' |\n' for row in rows)
text='''## Measured results and decision

**Keep.** The changes improve several greedy workloads and HQ encoding while
preserving every tested output byte. The strongest consistent result is the
1 MiB single-byte repeat: **1.186–1.205× at q10** and **1.244–1.250× at q11**
across cold, retained-output and writer APIs. Real-text HQ gains are generally
2–4%. These are measured results on this host, not a guarantee for every CPU or
input distribution.

The goal of being universally faster than other libraries is **not reached**.
In the final native-API matrix, mbrotli has the lowest mean in **48 of 96**
corpus/quality combinations, including **20 of 24 at q9–q11**. It has disjoint
95% timing intervals ahead of every competitor in **44** combinations. The
original had 48 lowest means and 43 disjoint leads: this patch improves useful
workloads, but does not establish a broad change in the overall ranking.

### Before/after with identical Rust API boundaries

Cold timings below include construction, allocation and disposal. Speed is the
geometric mean of paired `before / after` ratios; brackets are a bootstrap 95%
interval over the 16 paired batches. Times are arithmetic means. The output
column is identical before and after.

'''
selected=[('repeated-1m',10,'Single-byte repeat, 1 MiB'),('repeated-1m',11,'Single-byte repeat, 1 MiB'),('alice29',8,'Alice, 152,089 B'),('alice29',11,'Alice, 152,089 B'),('binary-64k',9,'Structured binary, 64 KiB'),('random-64k',9,'Random, 64 KiB'),('tiny-text',10,'Tiny text, 44 B'),('tiny-text',11,'Tiny text, 44 B')]
text+=table(['Input / quality','Before (ms)','After (ms)','Speed [95% interval]','Output (B)'],[(f'{label}, q{q}',f"{float(primary[c,q,'cold']['before_ns'])/1e6:.5f}",f"{float(primary[c,q,'cold']['after_ns'])/1e6:.5f}",ratio(primary[c,q,'cold'])+' ['+interval(primary[c,q,'cold'])+']',primary[c,q,'cold']['compressed_bytes']) for c,q,label in selected])
text+='''
API mode matters. For example, the large cold q8 Alice gain largely disappears
when its workspace is retained. The structured-binary q9 writer is slightly
slower despite its cold gain.

'''
text+=table(['Input / quality','Cold speed','Retained-output speed','4 KiB writer speed'],[(f'{label}, q{q}',*(ratio(primary[c,q,m]) for m in ['cold','reused','writer'])) for c,q,label in selected[:6]])
text+='''
The primary matrix's lowest point estimate is **0.956×** for reused q7 random
1 MiB, with interval **0.926–0.989×**. The q9 structured-binary writer is
**0.965× [0.930–0.998×]**, and the 44-byte q5 writer is
**0.965× [0.954–0.975×]**. Every primary point estimate is above 0.95×, but some
intervals admit larger regressions; this is not an uncertainty-aware universal
5% regression guarantee. No samples or cases were removed to hide those losses.

All **330 paired case summaries**, including timings, intervals, bytes and
retained capacity, are in [paired-summary.csv](encoder-optimization-2026-09-14/paired-summary.csv).
The raw [cold](encoder-optimization-2026-09-14/paired-cold.csv),
[retained-output](encoder-optimization-2026-09-14/paired-reused.csv), and
[writer](encoder-optimization-2026-09-14/paired-writer.csv) samples cover every
quality and primary corpus.

### Comparison with other libraries

These are the final cold native-API results. A relative rate above 1 means
mbrotli is faster than C. Counts describe this matrix, whose eight corpora have
equal weight; they are not a production workload distribution.

'''
ranking=read('competitor-summary.csv')
text+=table(['Quality','Lowest mean before / 8','Lowest mean after / 8','Disjoint leads after / 8','Median rate vs C after'],[(r['quality'],r['before_lowest_mean'],r['after_lowest_mean'],r['after_disjoint_intervals'],f"{float(r['after_median_speed_relative_to_c']):.3f}×") for r in ranking])
text+='''
[Before](encoder-optimization-2026-09-14/comparison-before.csv) and
[after](encoder-optimization-2026-09-14/comparison-after.csv) contain all 432
native measurements, their intervals, throughput and compressed sizes. Output
sizes match the before run in every row, including the unchanged competitors.
Native timings are separate processes and can drift with the host; use the
paired trials above to assess this patch's effect. For example, final native
tiny-HQ times are higher than the earlier baseline while their C controls also
rose; the contemporaneous paired tiny-HQ results are essentially unchanged.

The root Criterion suite additionally compares **matching C streaming FINISH
semantics**, exact bytes and API mode. Selected final results are:

'''
root={r['case']:r for r in read('root-criterion.csv')}
root_cases=[('cold',10,'repeated-1MiB','mbrotli','Cold single-byte repeat, 1 MiB'),('cold',11,'repeated-1MiB','mbrotli','Cold single-byte repeat, 1 MiB'),('streaming',9,'vendor-alice29.txt','mbrotli-writer','Alice writer'),('streaming',11,'vendor-alice29.txt','mbrotli-writer','Alice writer'),('cold',8,'incompressible-1MiB','mbrotli','Cold random, 1 MiB'),('cold',9,'incompressible-1MiB','mbrotli','Cold random, 1 MiB')]
rows=[]
for mode,q,corpus,implementation,label in root_cases:
 c=root[f'{mode}/q{q}/c-brotli/{corpus}'];m=root[f'{mode}/q{q}/{implementation}/{corpus}']
 rows.append((f'{label}, q{q}',f"{float(c['mean_ns'])/1e6:.3f}",f"{float(m['mean_ns'])/1e6:.3f}",f"{float(c['mean_ns'])/float(m['mean_ns']):.3f}×",m['compressed_bytes']))
text+=table(['Case','C (ms)','mbrotli (ms)','Rate vs C','Output (B)'],rows)
text+='''
The large random cases make the remaining gap concrete: C wins at q8 and q9.
[All 16 root Criterion measurements](encoder-optimization-2026-09-14/root-criterion.csv)
include intervals and throughput. HQ groups use their repository policy of
10 samples, 1 second warmup and a 3 second measurement target; other selected
groups use 20 samples and the command-line 0.1/0.3 second targets.

### Additional corpora

Six unmodified vendor files were checked with 12 alternating cold pairs each at
q5–q11. Every output matched the baseline bytes. Selected speed ratios follow;
all qualities and intervals remain in the summary and
[raw additional-corpus samples](encoder-optimization-2026-09-14/paired-heldout.csv).

'''
corpora=['lcet10.txt','plrabn12.txt','mapsdatazrh','random_org_10k.bin','quickfox_repeated','compressed_file']
text+=table(['Corpus','Input (B)','q7','q8','q9','q10','q11'],[(c,heldout[c,7]['input_bytes'],*(ratio(heldout[c,q]) for q in [7,8,9,10,11])) for c in corpora])
text+='''
The maps corpus improves **1.127× [1.104–1.151×] at q8** and
**1.117× [1.089–1.148×] at q9**. Already-compressed data at q11 regresses to
**0.971× [0.962–0.980×]**. The repeated phrase is essentially unchanged at HQ;
the much larger single-byte-repeat gain should not be generalized to every
repetitive input.

### Memory and final profiles

Measured retained capacity is unchanged for greedy cases. The HQ primary cases
add **6,144 bytes** for non-tiny inputs and **zero** for cold tiny inputs; the
10,000-byte held-out input adds 5,888 bytes. Larger capacity remains retained
when a later block is shorter. Retained capacity counts requested library
storage, not resident physical pages.

Fresh-process peak RSS, measured with GNU `time` over retained-output calls,
rises by **0.16–0.51 MiB** across the 15 measured cases (median of three runs
per side). This includes executable, runtime and allocator effects and is not
attributed solely to the price cache. Peak live requested bytes and post-release
allocator RSS were not isolated. Selected median process peaks are:

'''
rss=defaultdict(list)
for r in read('peak-rss.csv'):rss[int(r['quality']),r['corpus'],r['implementation']].append(int(r['peak_rss_kib'])/1024)
text+=table(['Case','Before peak RSS (MiB)','After peak RSS (MiB)'],[(f'{c}, q{q}',*(f'{statistics.median(rss[q,c,v]):.2f}' for v in ['before','after'])) for q,c in [(8,'random-1m'),(9,'random-1m'),(9,'repeated-1m'),(10,'random-1m'),(11,'random-1m')]])
text+='''
[All process-memory samples](encoder-optimization-2026-09-14/peak-rss.csv) and the
paired capacity columns preserve the distinction between these measurements.
The [final all-quality profiles](encoder-optimization-2026-09-14/profiles-after.csv)
still concentrate in search: q9 backward references occupy 58.58% of inclusive
profiled elapsed time, versus 59.33% before; q10 shortest-path search occupies
62.94%, versus 61.54%. These time-budgeted profiles redistribute work and call
counts as speed changes. Their percentages do not establish a speedup; the
un-instrumented timings above do.

The decision is to keep the measured text/search and long-copy improvements,
with the small regressions and memory costs above recorded. Future changes
should rerun this matrix without automatically replacing its baseline, and
should measure the caller's actual corpus and deployment CPU. q4–q8 and large
incompressible q9 inputs remain useful optimization targets.

'''
report=Path('docs/benchmarks/encoder-optimization-2026-09-14.md')
s=report.read_text();marker='## Measurement contract\n';assert marker in s
s=s.replace(marker,text+marker,1)
report.write_text(s)
